title: Rohit Sharma & Shubman Gill — 255-Run Opening Partnership
description: Phase-wise analysis of a 255-run opening partnership in 26.2 overs at Guwahati, highlighting scoring velocity, phase momentum, contribution share, and partnership acceleration.
visualizationMethod: Phase-wise trend + Over-by-Over line progression + Contribution donut breakdown
dataUsed: Ball-by-ball delivery event logs (Source: CricRadio Data Portal)
matchContext: India vs West Indies — 2nd ODI, Guwahati | 1st Wicket Opening Stand (Target Chase: India needed only 151 runs from 142 balls after opening stand of 255/1 in 26.2 overs)
datasetDescription: Delivery-level ball-by-ball event log capturing bowler spell details, delivery trajectory, batter strike rotation, boundary values, and over-by-over match progression.
methodology: Segmented innings into Phase 1 (Overs 1–10), Middle Phase (Overs 11–20), and Acceleration Phase (Overs 21–26.2). Calculated phase-wise strike rates, dot-ball pressure percentages, scoring burst points, and individual partnership contribution shares.
objective: Examine how the opening stand systematically dismantled field settings, maintained boundary momentum, and accelerated across distinct match phases.
keyMetrics: Total Partnership Runs: 255 Runs off 158 Balls (RR: 9.68 | SR: 161.4)
Rohit Sharma Contribution: 101 Runs (39.6% share | 10 Fours, 6 Sixes)
Shubman Gill Contribution: 145 Runs (56.9% share | 17 Fours, 6 Sixes)
Extras in Stand: 9 Runs (3.5% share)
Boundary Value: 180 Runs off Boundaries (70.6% of total | 27 Fours, 12 Sixes)
Rotation Runs: 75 Runs (29.4% of total | Singles: 52, Twos: 7, Dot Balls: 69)
Phase 1 (Overs 1–10): 92 Runs off 60 legal balls | SR: 153.3 | Dot Ball %: 53.3% | 70 Boundary Runs (76.1%)
Middle Phase (Overs 11–20): 96 Runs off 60 legal balls | SR: 160.0 | Dot Ball %: 43.3% | 60 Boundary Runs (66.7%)
Acceleration Phase (Overs 21–26.2): 67 Runs off 38 legal balls | SR: 176.3 | Dot Ball %: 28.9% | 50 Boundary Runs (74.6%)
Major Scoring Bursts: 8th (17 runs), 10th (17 runs), 16th (16 runs), 17th (17 runs), and 25th overs (18 runs)
keyInsights: The partnership accelerated systematically from 153.3 SR in the opening Powerplay to 176.3 SR during the acceleration phase.
Dot-ball percentage dropped consistently from 53.3% in overs 1–10 down to 28.9% in overs 21–26.2, maintaining intense pressure on the bowling unit.
Boundary hitting generated 70.6% of total partnership runs (180 runs), preventing defensive setup deliveries.
Shubman Gill provided the primary scoring thrust with 145 partnership runs (56.9% share), complemented by Rohit Sharma's calculated 101 runs (39.6% share).
limitations: Delivery speeds and release angles recorded from broadcast feed coding; fielding placement shifts modeled from video playback rather than GPS player-tracking sensors.
coordinateType: Video-tagged delivery event logs with manual phase boundary segmentation.

title: Sanju Samson & Abhishek Sharma — Inside India's Explosive 1st-Wicket Partnership
visualizationMethod: Batter side-by-side comparison + Dual wagon wheels + Over progression trajectory
dataUsed: Ball-by-ball delivery event logs (Source: CricRadio Data Portal)
matchContext: India vs Zimbabwe — T20 International Series | 1st Wicket Opening Stand (Ended at 9.5 overs: Sanju Samson 34 c Abhishek b Brar)
datasetDescription: Delivery-level ball-by-ball scoring logs capturing bowler line, length, batter footwork, contact quality (clean hit vs false shot), and 360-degree shot trajectory.
methodology: Calculated False Shot Induced Rate (FSIR) (Edges + Beaten + Mistimed / Balls Faced) * 100, over-by-over scoring velocity, and asymmetric partnership contribution share.
objective: Examine ultra-aggressive partnership dynamics, asymmetric strike distribution, boundary frequency, and over-by-over momentum spikes.
keyMetrics: Partnership Runs: 142 Runs off 59 Balls (Combined SR: 240.68 | RR: 14.44 RPO)
Abhishek Sharma: 108 Runs off 34 Balls (SR: 317.65 | 13 Fours, 6 Sixes | 94 Boundary Runs | 79.66% Boundary %)
Sanju Samson: 34 Runs off 25 Balls (SR: 136.00 | 3 Fours, 1 Six | 18 Boundary Runs | 36.00% Boundary %)
Partnership Share: Abhishek Sharma 76.06% | Sanju Samson 23.94%
Total Boundaries: 16 Fours & 7 Sixes (112 Runs off Boundaries | 78.87% of partnership)
Dot Ball Pressure: 19 Dot Balls faced out of 59 deliveries (32.20% Dot Ball %)
False Shot Control: Only 6 False Shots across 59 balls (10.17% False Shot %)
Abhishek False Shot %: 5.88% (Elite control at 317.65 SR) | Samson False Shot %: 12.00%
Partnership Turning Point: Over 1.4 to Over 2.1 — 27 Runs in 6 consecutive balls (SR: 450.00 | 4 Fours, 2 Sixes), accelerating stand from 2/3 to 29/9
keyInsights: Abhishek Sharma executed one of modern T20I's most destructive assault phases, scoring 108 runs off 34 balls at a strike rate of 317.65 with only 5.88% false shot rate.
Boundary runs accounted for 78.87% of all partnership runs (112 runs), dismantling opposition powerplay fielding plans within 2 overs.
Sanju Samson played a disciplined anchoring role (34 off 25 balls), ensuring continuous strike rotation back to Abhishek.
The decisive turning point occurred between overs 1.4 and 2.1, where 27 runs were extracted in 6 consecutive deliveries at a 450.00 strike rate.
limitations: Delivery speeds derived from broadcast frame interval analysis; pitch moisture and surface friction conditions qualitative.
coordinateType: Delivery-by-delivery video tagging with pitch corridor and wagon wheel radial quadrant tagging.

title: Shafali Verma — Scoring Impact by Pitching Length
visualizationMethod: 3D Isometric Pitch Strip with length-wise metric badges & false shot matrix
dataUsed: Delivery-level pitch coordinates (Source: CricRadio Data Portal)
matchContext: India vs Sri Lanka — Final Match, Women's Asia Cup T20 2026 | Batting Analysis
datasetDescription: 39 delivery logs tagged with pitch landing longitudinal distance from batting stumps, lateral deviation, shot response, and batter execution outcome.
methodology: Categorized deliveries into 6 longitudinal length corridors: Full Toss, Yorker, Half Volley, Good Length, Back of Length, and Short Length. Computed Runs, Balls, False Shot %, and Share of Total Runs for each zone.
objective: Identify scoring productivity and tactical vulnerabilities across distinct bowling length zones in a continental tournament final.
keyMetrics: Total Innings Summary: 68 Runs off 39 Balls (Strike Rate: 174.36)
Boundary Count: 9 Fours & 2 Sixes (11 Boundaries | 48 Boundary Runs)
Overall False Shot %: 17.95%
Back of Length (Primary Scoring Zone): 31 Runs off 15 Balls (SR: 206.67 | 13.33% False Shot % | 45.59% of Innings Runs)
Good Length: 21 Runs off 13 Balls (SR: 161.54 | 23.08% False Shot % | 30.88% of Innings Runs)
Half Volley: 9 Runs off 6 Balls (SR: 150.00 | 0.00% False Shot % | 13.24% of Innings Runs)
Short Length: 5 Runs off 2 Balls (SR: 250.00 | 0.00% False Shot % | 7.35% of Innings Runs)
Full Toss: 2 Runs off 1 Ball (100.00% False Shot % | 2.94% of Innings Runs)
Yorker: 0 Runs off 2 Balls (50.00% False Shot % | 0.00% of Innings Runs)
keyInsights: Back-of-length deliveries were exploited most brutally, producing 45.59% of her total runs (31 runs off 15 balls) at an explosive 206.67 strike rate.
Good length deliveries generated the highest tactical resistance (23.08% false shot rate), yet she counter-attacked to score 21 runs off 13 balls (161.54 SR).
Zero false shots conceded against half volley (9 off 6) and short length (5 off 2) balls, punishing any bowler missing their primary length marks.
Demonstrates how spatial pitch length zoning pinpoints a batter's optimal attack corridor and defensive compromises in high-pressure matches.
limitations: Pitch landing coordinates were manually tagged from broadcast multi-angle video replays using a standardized 6-zone length grid, rather than automated ball-tracking sensor telemetry.
coordinateType: Manually tagged broadcast video coordinates mapped to calibrated 22-yard pitch zone strips.
